purpose: A documentation section heading that is also the link to itself. The whole text links to its own `id`, so a reader can copy the URL to the section; a rule under the text and a chain glyph after it appear on hover and keyboard focus without taking layout. The click goes through `useHeadingNav`, so the page decides how to scroll; with no page it falls back to the native hash jump. MDX renderers and hand-composed pages both render headings through it, so the two authoring paths cannot drift.
useWhen: Every `h2`–`h4` on a docs page that the page rail lists.
Section headings on a designed docs page composed in Vue.
related: DocOnThisPage` — the rail that points at the ids.
DocProse` — skips `[data-doc-anchor]` in its link rules.
bestPractices: Give every heading a stable, slug-like `id`.
Without an `id` the heading renders plain text with no anchor — a link to nowhere is never drawn.
